vulnerability.title: Jenkins doToggleCollapse accepts GET requests, allowing CSRF to toggle a user's sidepanel widget state

fixed_releases.verified_content: The 2.500 release commit cb753134 has 923cdbc1 as its only parent; the SECURITY-3498 fix 84ef1a4d is the parent of 4a9a3ecd, which is the parent of 923cdbc1 (git merge-base --is-ancestor 84ef1a4d cb753134 exits 0). At cb753134 doToggleCollapse carries @POST (line 4168) and pane.jelly renders the trigger as class="collapse post" (line 64). The CNA record also lists LTS 2.492.2 as unaffected; that backport was not fetched or asserted.

fix_commits.branch: 2.492.x LTS release commit (backport not fetched, ancestry not asserted)

severity.numeric_level_rationale: NVD publishes a single CVSS 3.1 metric, 5.4 MEDIUM, from the Secondary source (CISA-ADP); there is no Primary metric. OSV/GHSA repeats the same 5.4 vector and records MODERATE, which is the same medium band. The CNA container has no CVSS metric. Every published severity level is medium, so the level is consistent and the score is not averaged.

vulnerability.category_l2: A state-changing endpoint without @POST is routed for GET, so a cross-site request from the victim's browser toggles the victim's pane collapse state

description: Jenkins exposes /toggleCollapse, implemented by Jenkins.doToggleCollapse, to toggle the collapsed/expanded state of sidepanel widgets such as Build Queue and Build Executor Status. At 2.441 the method (4214-4221) has no @POST or @RequirePOST annotation, so Stapler routes GET requests to it. It reads the paneId request parameter and calls PaneStatusProperties.forCurrentUser().toggleCollapsed(paneId): for a logged-in user this adds or removes the attacker-chosen id in that user's persisted collapsed set (PersistedList owned by the user property, whose save() calls user.save()), and for an anonymous visitor it writes the same id into the session attribute jenkins_pane__collapsed. Because the state change is reachable with GET, an attacker page can embed an or link to /toggleCollapse?paneId=... and the victim's browser performs the toggle without a crumb, which Jenkins enforces for POST requests. The impact is integrity of the victim's UI preferences (the published CVSS counts I:L and A:L, C:N). The 2.500 fix 84ef1a4d adds @POST to the method and converts both UI triggers (pane.jelly and executors.jelly) to class="collapse post" with the lib.form.link.link adjunct; its regression test JenkinsTest.testPaneToggleCollapse asserts that a GET to toggleCollapse is rejected (404).

critical_operation.description: The state-changing handler has no @POST (or @RequirePOST) annotation and no permission check, so Stapler dispatches GET requests to it. The paneId query parameter is passed to PaneStatusProperties.toggleCollapsed, which mutates and persists the victim's collapsed-widget set.

entry_point.description: Any cross-site GET such as /toggleCollapse?paneId=buildQueue (the UI emits it as a plain <a> href from pane.jelly); because the method is unannotated, the GET reaches the handler without a crumb check.

trace.description: doToggleCollapse has no @POST and no permission check, so GET is routed to the state-changing handler
forCurrentUser returns the current user's PaneStatusProperties, or a session-backed fallback when no user is logged in

the persisted collection's owner save() calls user.save(), so the toggle is stored in the victim's profile

source_crosscheck.notes: The CNA, NVD, OSV and the GitHub advisory agree on the mechanism (CSRF allowing a cross-site request to toggle a user's sidepanel widget collapse state) and on the fixed releases (2.500 weekly, 2.492.2 LTS). NVD publishes no Primary metric; its only metric is the CISA-ADP Secondary 5.4 MEDIUM, which OSV/GHSA repeats as 5.4 MODERATE, and the CNA has no metric, so all published levels are medium. CWE-352 is recorded by NVD's Secondary source and by GHSA; the CNA lists none. The GHSA ECOSYSTEM weekly range introduced=2.493 conflicts with the CNA text and the OSV GIT range (introduced 0); this dataset follows the CNA and GIT range and records the conflict. This root cause is distinct from the previously promoted jenkins entries: CVE-2024-23897 (CLI arbitrary file read), CVE-2024-23898 (CLI WebSocket hijacking), CVE-2024-43045 (My Views permission check), CVE-2025-27622 (agent config.xml redaction), CVE-2025-27623 (view config.xml redaction) and CVE-2025-27625 (backslash open redirect); it is a missing POST restriction on a state-changing Jenkins endpoint.

independent_corrections_accepted: The reviewer independently confirmed the unannotated handler, the paneId sink and the fixed tree, and added the widget call sites lib/hudson/executors.jelly:140 (l:pane id="executors") and lib/hudson/queue.jelly:48 (l:pane id="buildQueue"), which correspond to the Build Executor Status and Build Queue widgets named in the advisory.

The reviewer also checked the upstream tags directly: jenkins-2.499 has no @POST (Jenkins.java:4168) while jenkins-2.492.2 (4166) and jenkins-2.500 (4169) carry it, which independently confirms the affected/fixed boundary and the 2.492.2 LTS backport that this dossier did not assert from local ancestry.
The reviewer noted the CNA record supplies neither CVSS nor CWE, and that no independent non-reporter PoC exists (CISA SSVC exploitation=none, EPSS 0.00441), which keeps the grade at B.
review.duplicate_check: The reviewer compared CVE-2024-23897, CVE-2024-23898, CVE-2024-43045, CVE-2025-27622, CVE-2025-27623 and CVE-2025-27625 and found no duplicate: different advisory ids, fix commits (84ef1a4d vs 4a9a3ecd/923cdbc1), endpoints and code paths.
required_before_promotion: An independent reviewer must read Jenkins.doToggleCollapse at 2.441 and confirm it lacks @POST and performs no permission check.
An independent reviewer must confirm PaneStatusProperties.toggleCollapsed mutates the victim's persisted state (or the session fallback) for the supplied paneId.
An independent reviewer must confirm 84ef1a4d is the fix, is contained in the 2.500 release, and that the fixed tree annotates the method @POST and converts the trigger to a POST link.
An independent reviewer must confirm the affected range (weekly <=2.499, LTS <=2.492.1) and that 2.441 is inside it.
An independent reviewer must confirm all published severity levels are medium (5.4) and record CWE-352.
An independent reviewer must confirm the mechanism is distinct from the promoted jenkins entries.
No formal reviews.jsonl row may be written until a named independent reviewer returns a verdict.

limitations: Static verification only; no Jenkins instance, HTTP request or browser was run.

The attack requires a victim to load an attacker-controlled page while the endpoint is reachable from the victim's browser (UI:R); the impact is limited to the victim's pane collapse preferences, as reflected by C:N/I:L/A:L.
The crumb-check exemption for GET is a property of Jenkins' request handling that is evidenced by the fix choosing @POST rather than a token check; it was not exercised against a running instance.
Only one location row is recorded (Jenkins.doToggleCollapse). The sink in PaneStatusProperties and the Jelly trigger are recorded as trace/entry-point evidence.
The LTS backport and the 2.492.2 branch were not fetched into the local mirror; LTS ancestry is recorded from OSV and the CNA record, not asserted locally.
The GHSA ECOSYSTEM range introduced=2.493 conflicts with the CNA and the OSV GIT range; the conflict is documented, not resolved silently.
open_questions: Whether other unannotated state-changing handlers share the same pattern was not enumerated beyond the advisory's scope.
Anonymous visitors hit the session fallback rather than the persisted user property; the advisory describes the affected users generally, and both paths accept an attacker-supplied paneId.
